question: What is the standard length of an Olympic-size swimming pool?
solution:
The correct answer is __**50 metres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **Olympic-size swimming pool** is a swimming pool that conforms to the specifications set by the **International Swimming Federation (FINA)**.
 
• The length of an Olympic-size swimming pool is **50 metres**.
 
• It is used for the **Olympic Games** and other international competitions.
 
• The width of the pool is **25 metres**.
 
• The pool is divided into **8 lanes**, each lane being 2.5 metres wide.
 
• The minimum depth of the pool is **2 metres**.
 
• These dimensions allow for competitive swimming events such as **freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **70 metres__**

 __
 
• This length is not a standard dimension for any competitive swimming pool.
 
• Most competitive pools adhere to the dimensions set by governing bodies like **FINA**.
 
 
 
• **60 metres__**
 __
 
• 60 metres is also not a standard length for competitive swimming pools.
 
• Standard lengths are typically **25 metres** (short course) or **50 metres** (long course).
 
 
 
• **40 metres__**
 
 
• 40 metres is shorter than the standard lengths used in international competitions.
 
• Such lengths are not typically used for competitive swimming events.
